label: canon4-je-n5
_why: canon-4rung (§10.69) with ONE change: the research-event parameters restored to the six-rung canon's level on the four-rung anchors — RULED 2026-09-03: marks by the UNLOCKED rung's era t1 25k · t2 75k · t3 235k workers at the base method's staffing in the predecessor rung (rule-D keys 4/5 → 235k), 60-month bars per stage, ONE ×0.5 multiplier on arms/artillery/explosives/munition/synthetics, every source counted in fully staffed levels, every JE naming its sources and live figures, the art academy counted at its real per-level employment (config/mod_config.canon4-je.json; field diff against the canon: the research_events block only). User's hypothesis (2026-09-03): 'when we bring them back to the old level (or slightly lower), this gets balanced to better equilibria'. Measured cause (F101): the four-rung book fires ~620–690 JE completions per run over ~150 countries (GBR 15–25, USA 3–9, FRA 0–3; 13–20 of 40 covered technologies) against the six-rung canon's ~4,700–4,800 over ~335 countries (GBR 79–86, USA 80–82, FRA 8–34), and its technology pace is exactly vanilla's (GBR 163 techs at 1935 = vanilla's 163; the six-rung canon 196) — make_tier4_config had re-derived the thresholds ×4 per rung from a 30k base and halved the tick. n=3; 1836 → 1936.1.1; compared against canon-4rung (20260903_000418 growth seeds + 20260903_094941, the same book) and vanilla n=16. ⭐ PLUS THE MILITARY CHANNELS (user-ruled 2026-09-03, §10.69): unit-type technologies get the WAR entry (a general of ours with ≥50 mobilised battalions on a front against an enemy holding the technology, no casualties clause, 6 monthly ticks per stage — 8 entries), the percussion-cap first rung anchors on SMALL-ARMS consumption (≥900/wk, the British market's 1846 level; the unlocked good's own demand was rejected — it cannot precede supply), the explosives first rung rides fertilizer's staple-crops anchor, industry tick speed, no naval entries. Emitted: 51 technologies (43 industry, 8 war) → 153 journal entries.

_delta: vs canon-4rung: the research_events block only (thresholds, bar lengths, the military channels: war_channel unit_types, naval_channel false, war_gate flat 50 / no casualties / 6-month bars, consumption_thresholds small_arms 900, munition anchored on small-arms consumption, the explosives first rung on staple crops). _predictions.P1_firings: JE completions per run ≥ 1,500 (canon-4rung 620–690); Britain: ≥ 45% of e2-unlocking and ≥ 40% of e3-unlocking rule-A technologies with at least one stage fired (the F101.2 replay: 45% / 41%); FRA ≥ 5, USA ≥ 30 completions.
_predictions.P2_pace: Technology pace ahead of vanilla: GBR technologies held at 1900 ≥ 135 (canon-4rung 128 = vanilla 125) and at 1935 ≥ 175 (163).
_predictions.P3_frontier: Earlier frontier rungs: British plastics glassworks and rubber-grip tooling levels at 1905 above the canon's (10–12 / 9–56); shortlist e0 headcount at 1935 below the canon's 695–850k; the e1 rung no longer the largest at 1935 in at least one seed.
_predictions.P4_gdp: World GDP 0.90–1.05× vanilla (the six-rung canon's JEs raised GDP; the four-rung book's capacity pricing may absorb it).
_predictions.P6_stall: Stall count reported (family 1 in 7); a stall is an outcome, not a defect.
_predictions.P7_risk: If P1 passes and P3 fails, faster technology does not by itself move the ladder — the price/wage death mechanism still gates it (F97).
_predictions.P8_military: The war channel fires for MAJORS at war: ≥1 PMR_JE|…|<unit-type tech> completion for GBR, FRA or PRU in ≥3 of 5 runs (canon-4rung: 0 war entries existed). Percussion cap completions for GBR ≥ 1 in ≥ 2 of 5 runs (canon-4rung: 0 in six runs — Britain clears 900 small arms/wk from the mid-1840s but researches percussion cap within a few years of 1836, so the 60-month bar may still lose the race; a zero is the race, not the trigger, IF the bar is seen ticking in an error-free log).

_watch: 5-minute smoke check: error.log for any `market`/`mg:` scope error from a progress bar (the consumption term is unverified in-game) and for `pmr_wargate_` variable errors; the first PMR_JE|…|percussion_cap line, whichever country, proves the small-arms consumption bar ticks
5-minute smoke check incl. a look at a research JE's text in the mirror if any loc error is logged (the ScriptValue data function inside a JE is unverified in-game)
first run: JE completions (PMR_JE) by country, GBR/FRA/USA technologies held at 1900 vs the canon, first_run_decomp, company_check
_cost: 5 × 1836→1936, ~2.6 h each: ~13 h. LAUNCHED 2026-09-03 with the user's explicit go-ahead ("Save this, build this, go with n=5") after the small-arms anchor ruling.
_caveats: n=3 against n=4 on the same book: the JE-count and tech-pace predictions resolve; GDP under ~10% does not.

The four-rung tree covers 40 technologies with JEs against the six-rung canon's 201 today (378 at the time of its runs), so 'back to the old level' restores the per-JE parameters, not the number of JEs.

KNOWN DEFECT, all five runs (found 1838 of run 1, not stopped by the user's instruction): two of the eight war entries are naval-tree technologies — power_of_the_purse and landing_craft unlock MARINES, which vanilla files under land unit types — so a naval technology can be granted on an army front condition. Read the army channel as the other six; list it as a confound on naval-technology pace. Fix (exclude combat_unit_group_marines) queued behind the batch, L10.
